title: Senior's toolkit: authentication and hardening
summary: hydra for testing your own login limits, ASP.NET Core's rate limiter and Identity's PasswordHasher, the security headers check, and structured logging that redacts.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: authentication and hardening
steps.body: The tools for proving a login resists guessing, storing passwords the standard way, and checking the headers and logs a scan or an auditor will look at.

toolkit.cmd: hydra -l USER -P wordlist -s PORT HOST http-post-form 'PATH:BODY:F=failure text'
toolkit.what: Online password guessing against a login form: the way to prove your rate limit and lockout work, on your own staging system.
flags: text that means a failed attempt (S= for success text)

toolkit.what: ASP.NET Core's built-in rate limiting middleware (Microsoft.AspNetCore.RateLimiting): fixed window, sliding window, token bucket and concurrency limiters, partitioned by whatever key you choose.
flags: one counter per key (address, user, API key)
apply a policy to an endpoint or group

toolkit.what: ASP.NET Core Identity's password hasher, usable on its own: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 with a random salt and a versioned format, and SuccessRehashNeeded when a stored hash should be upgraded.
The 10-second header check before a scan: which security headers are there, and what the Server header gives away. securityheaders.com does the same for public sites.

toolkit.cmd: logger.LogWarning("Sign-in failed for {UserId} from {Ip}", id, ip)
toolkit.what: Structured logging: values travel as named properties (encoded by the sink, searchable in the SIEM) instead of being glued into the message. Add HTTP logging with redaction for request details.
flags: a named property, not string interpolation
log only the headers you list
mark data as personal or secret and redact it
toolkit.example:
builder.Services.AddHttpLogging(o => { o.LoggingFields = HttpLoggingFields.RequestPath | HttpLoggingFields.ResponseStatusCode; });
logger.LogWarning("Sign-in failed for {UserName} from {Ip}", login.Username, ctx.Connection.RemoteIpAddress);

steps.prompt: Match each tool or API to its job.
pairs: proves a login can or cannot be guessed
puts a rate limit policy on an endpoint
says a stored password hash should be upgraded
a structured property instead of string gluing

steps.prompt: Test the lab's login: stop at the first hit, and treat this text as failure.
A rate limiter rejects requests with its default status. Why do teams set `RejectionStatusCode = 429`?
options: The default is 503, which looks like an outage to monitoring and to clients; 429 tells a client to slow down and lets alerts count throttling separately
